body.statement: For finite alphabets and fixed rational or real-algebraic \(p\), \(\mu\), and \(\pi\) with \(\mathcal K(p)\ne\varnothing\), \(\mathsf{CAD}_\eta\) terminates on \(\exists q\,[q\in\mathcal K(p)\wedge v=V_\pi(q)]\) and returns all connected components of \(\Theta_I(p)\) as closed intervals or singleton points with exact real-algebraic endpoints; alternatively it returns disjoint certified rational \(\eta\)-enclosures of every component and endpoint. For a presentation with \(N\) real variables, \(s\) polynomial constraints, and maximum degree \(d\), classical sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition uses at most \((sd)^{2^{O(N)}}\) arithmetic operations, with exact coefficient arithmetic, and the same bound controls the number of cells examined.
body.justification: The result turns fixed-law sharpness into a terminating exact computation rather than a local numerical optimization claim.
body.gap: Duarte et al. (2024) motivate certified polynomial optimization for discrete causal models; this theorem specializes exact real elimination to the coupled weak-shadow value image and reports all connected components.
body.consumer: An auditor can reproduce exact algebraic policy-value bounds for a finite sepsis table or request certified enclosures at tolerance \(\eta\).
body.proof_tex:
We use exact sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition, with \(\mathrm{lem{:}effective\text{-}real\text{-}cad}\) as the published classical substrate, and derive the specialization to the weak-shadow fiber.

Fix rational or real-algebraic \(p\), \(\mu\), and \(\pi\).  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}positivity}\), every \(\mu_t(a\mid g)\) appearing in an importance ratio is nonzero.  The field generated over \(\mathbb Q\) by the finitely many coordinates of \(p\), \(\mu\), and \(\pi\), and by their permitted reciprocals, is therefore an effectively represented real-algebraic coefficient field.  In coordinates \(q=(q_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}\), membership in \(\mathcal K(p)\) is the conjunction of
\[
 q_\omega\geq0,\qquad \sum_\omega q_\omega=1,\qquad O_\#q=p,
\]
the finite linear behavior equations, and the finite quadratic weak-shadow cross-products.  Furthermore,
\[
 v=V_\pi(q)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 v-\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}q_\omega\sum_{t=1}^H
 \rho_t^\pi(\omega)R_t(\omega)=0
\]
is one linear polynomial equation over that field.  Hence
\[
 \Phi(v)\equiv\exists(q_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}\,\bigl[q\in\mathcal K(p)\wedge v=V_\pi(q)\bigr]
\]
is a first-order real formula with \(N\) real variables, \(s\) polynomial constraints, and maximum degree \(d\) in the presentation stipulated by the theorem.

Apply the sign-invariant CAD result \(\mathrm{lem{:}effective\text{-}real\text{-}cad}\) to all input polynomials, ordering \(v\) as the uneliminated coordinate.  The algorithm terminates, performs exact arithmetic in the real-algebraic coefficient field, and produces an equivalent quantifier-free univariate sign formula for \(\Phi(v)\).  Its arithmetic-operation count is at most
\[
 (sd)^{2^{O(N)}}.
\]
Every examined CAD cell requires construction data, so the number of examined cells is bounded by the same asymptotic operation bound.

By \(\mathrm{def{:}identified\text{-}set}\), the truth set of \(\Phi\) is exactly \(\Theta_I(p)\).  A univariate quantifier-free sign formula can change truth value only at a real root of one of its finitely many nonzero projection polynomials.  Thus its truth set is a finite union of points and intervals with real-algebraic boundary points.  By \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}attainment}\), \(\Theta_I(p)\) is compact and hence closed and bounded.  After adjacent true CAD cells are merged, each connected component is consequently either a singleton or a closed interval, and every endpoint is real algebraic.

The exact CAD representation records each boundary root by a defining polynomial and exact sign or Thom data, so it gives exact endpoints.  For the enclosure alternative, let \(E\) be the finite set of distinct endpoints.  Exact comparison of real-algebraic numbers orders \(E\).  Because \(\eta>0\) and distinct members of \(E\) have positive separation, repeated rational bisection around each member produces rational intervals of width at most \(\eta\); refining further when necessary makes these intervals pairwise disjoint.  Exact sign evaluation at rational endpoints certifies that each interval contains its designated algebraic endpoint.  Reporting the paired endpoint enclosures, and the analogous enclosure for a singleton, gives the asserted certified \(\eta\)-description of every component.  This is a global value-image certificate: no local optimizer or convexity of \(\mathcal K(p)\) is used.
